item.title: It’s just a song: Philippine leader laughs off debate over Apec welcome track Anak
item.description: Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jnr has downplayed Beijing’s choice of music to greet him at the Apec summit, saying the debate about possible hidden meanings was overblown. A Chinese orchestra played the classic Philippine song “Anak”, which means child, when the Philippine presidential couple entered the hall for the welcome banquet in Shenzhen on Wednesday. The song, written by Freddie Aguilar, tells the tale of a young person’s rebellion against parental authority and subsequent... Fuente: South China Morning Post.
item.dc:creator: Fan Chen

item.title: Ghana's $60 million presidential jet purchase sparks controversy
item.description: Ghanaian President John Mahama is facing growing criticism over his government's recent purchase of a $60 million presidential jet. While in opposition, Mahama had criticised similar plans by the previous administration. The government in Accra is now defending the purchase, pointing to the country's improved economic situation. It argues that the question was never whether the ageing presidential aircraft should be replaced, but rather when the timing would be right. FRANCE 24's Justice Baidoo reports. Fuente: France 24 - English.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: A Summit Gives Putin the Win He Craves: Equal Stature With Superpowers
item.description: Standing alongside the U.S. and Chinese leaders, President Vladimir V. Putin secured a symbolic triumph in his long quest to restore Russia’s place as a global power. Fuente: The New York Times - World.
item.dc:creator: Paul Sonne

item.title: Cop31 live: ‘We didn’t come here to beg’, African ministers say as climate talks enter final day
item.description: Disagreements between rich polluting countries and everyone else threaten to push UN summit beyond its official end In a huddle outside the African group’s media conference this morning, Dr Zanetor Agyeman-Rawlings , Ghana’s environment minister and chair of the African group of negotiators, has laid out her thoughts on the proposed global electrification target that is now sitting as one of the agreements in the draft text of the “cover decision”. She said if electrification is included in the text without a means for African countries to develop electricity “then what you’re doing is… Fuente: The Guardian - Environment.
item.dc:creator: Matthew Pearce

item.title: Was the historic Shenzhen summit a political win or humiliation for Putin?
item.description: The world watched with bated breath Thursday as the presidents of China, Russia and the United States met for 90 minutes for an unprecedented trilateral summit in Shenzhen. Each leader came to the negotiating table with their own motivations. But Russia's Vladimir Putin was seen as walking away worse off than his counterparts, with some media outlets reporting the Kremlin leader was "humiliated" during the talks. Fuente: France 24 - English.
item.dc:creator: Sébastian SEIBT

item.title: Una periodista es apartada por China de la cumbre trilateral tras preguntar a Trump por el caso Nvidia durante su encuentro con Xi
item.description: Una reportera de la agencia Bloomberg fue apartada por las autoridades chinas del resto de prensa que cubrió las declaraciones iniciales del presidente de Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, en el marco de la cumbre trilateral con sus homólogos de Rusia, Vladimir Putin, y China, Xi Jinping, celebrada en Shenzhen.La decisión, que le impidió a la periodista Annmarie Hordern seguir la comparecencia, llegó después de que la misma lanzara una pregunta a Trump durante un encuentro anterior con Xi, según recoge una información enviada por la prensa acreditada en la Casa Blanca, que ha seguido al… Fuente: ABC España - Internacional.
item.dc:creator: EP

item.title: Rare EU-UK summit as Andy Burnham seeks to mend Brexit damage
item.description: UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham and the EU's top officials were set to announce deals to ease trade and youth mobility at a Brussels summit Friday, billed as a first step in a push to rebuild ties after Brexit. But in a potential spoiler for Burnham's "reset", Brussels said the deals coming into force would be conditional on reaching an agreement to cut university fees for EU students in Britain. FRANCE 24's International Affairs Editor Rochelle Ferguson Bouyahi tells us more. Fuente: France 24 - English.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: 'Coalition of the Willing': Ukraine's allies meet in Berlin after Trump-Putin-Xi talks
item.description: Ukraine's allies met Thursday for a "Coalition of the Willing" summit in Berlin with President Volodymyr Zelensky to stress solid wartime support for Kyiv and to push for a European role in any future peace talks. The meeting – co-hosted by the leaders of Germany, France and Britain – was being held shortly after unprecedented three-way talks in China between US President Donald Trump, Russia's Vladimir Putin and China's Xi Jinping. Fuente: France 24 - English.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Spain's leaders clash over corruption, economy in tense election debate
item.description: Spain's Socialist Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez acknowledged making "mistakes" as he faced off with his main conservative rival in a key debate on Thursday before an election next week that could leave the far right on the cusp of power. The pair clashed over the economy, housing, immigration, corruption, foreign policy, as well as policies towards women, repeatedly interrupting each other during the live televised showdown. Fuente: France 24 - English.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Iraqi forces strike compromise with powerful pro-Iran militia
item.description: Iraq has reached ​a compromise with the powerful Iran-backed militia Kataib Hezbollah, three senior security officials said, after Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi readied security forces to move against the group. Iraqi officials had accused the group of running a smuggling ring that siphoned off hundreds of millions ​of dollars' worth of ‌state-owned oil. Under the deal brokered by senior Shi'ite political leaders to avert a confrontation, government ⁠forces were expected to move into the group's stronghold of Jurf al-Sakhar on Friday. Fuente: France 24 - English.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Easing Back From Brexit: What to Expect at U.K. Summit With E.U.
item.description: Prime Minister Andy Burnham is in Brussels to announce a deal to reset Britain’s relationship with the European Union, a decade after it left the bloc. Fuente: The New York Times - World.
item.dc:creator: Jeanna Smialek and Michael D. Shear

item.title: Malaysia plans to resettle 10,000 Rohingya in Turkiye
item.description: Malaysia is seeking to resettle 10,000 Rohingya migrants in Turkey as part of efforts to resolve a long-running refugee challenge involving foreign asylum seekers, the majority from Myanmar, a senior official said on Friday. The announcement by Deputy Prime Minister Ahmad Zahid Hamidi comes a day after the UN’s top court, in a landmark ruling, said that Myanmar committed genocide against the ethnic minority. “Following my recent official working visit to the Republic of Turkiye, the Cabinet has... Publicado también por: South China Morning Post. Fuente: The Hindu - International.

item.title: Brussels, London eye 'reset' deal at Burnham's EU summit
item.description: British Prime Minister Andy Burnham is due to meet EU chiefs Ursula von der Leyen and Antonio Costa in Brussels on Friday for a summit aimed at resetting ties after the turbulent years surrounding Brexit. The two sides are hoping to strike several deals, with the talks expected to pave the way for closer cooperation in the future. FRANCE 24's Brussels correspondent Dave Keating explains the main issues on the agenda. Fuente: France 24 - English.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Mexican leader Sheinbaum’s 21-hour economy-class journey draws praise in China
item.description: Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum’s journey in economy class from Mexico City to Shenzhen for the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit has gone viral on Chinese social media. While most world leaders travelled to the southern Chinese city on chartered airliners or government aircraft, Sheinbaum arrived on Monday on a scheduled commercial flight. She flew on China Southern Airlines flight CZ8032, according to CARNOC, a Chinese aviation trade publication. The aircraft had a special blue,... Fuente: South China Morning Post.
item.dc:creator: Eve Qiao

item.title: 10 years on, Britain reopens the Brexit fight — this time embracing the E.U.
item.description: Prime Minister Andy Burnham is set to sign the most concrete unwinding of the severance since 2016, as more Britons say leaving the European Union was a mistake. Fuente: The Washington Post - World.
item.dc:creator: Steve Hendrix

item.title: Former French prime minister Dominique de Villepin announces presidential bid
item.description: France’s former conservative prime minister Dominique de Villepin, who served as former president Jacques Chirac’s foreign minister during the country’s steadfast opposition to the US-led invasion of Iraq in 2003, formally launched his presidential campaign Friday. But while De Villepin’s opposition to Israel’s Gaza campaign and assured analysis of international affairs has caught the eyes of younger voters, it remains to be seen if he can persuade them to cast a ballot for him. Fuente: France 24 - English.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE 24

item.title: The U.K. and EU hold a rare summit to strengthen ties
item.description: A decade after the people of Britain voted to leave the European Union, top EU officials are meeting with Prime Minister Andy Burnham on Friday, looking to mend more fences. Fuente: NPR - World.

item.description: Iraqi security forces deployed ​in the Kataib Hezbollah stronghold of Jurf al-Sakhar, state media said on Friday, under a compromise deal brokered by Shi'ite politicians. Iraq's prime minister ordered a security intervention earlier this week after accusing the Iran-backed militia of smuggling state-owned oil worth ⁠hundreds of millions of dollars. item.description: Chinese President Xi Jinping and US President Donald Trump met this week in Shenzhen on the sidelines of the Apec meeting, where they discussed introducing shared guard rails on artificial intelligence amid growing numbers of AI-enabled cyber hacking incidents affecting banks and governments worldwide. In the last part of a three-part series profiling Chinese organisations at the forefront of efforts to ensure that innovation does not come at the expense of safety in China’s AI industry, we... item.title: Taiwan flags thousands of Meta accounts over Chinese election interference campaign
item.description: Taiwanese officials have expressed concern that Beijing, which claims democratically governed Taiwan as its own territory, is intensifying online efforts to sway voters before the elections. Fuente: The Jerusalem Post - International.

item.description: The two Prime Ministers will inaugurate several energy-related projects; Nepal’s PM will also call on President Murmu during his official visit Fuente: The Hindu - International.

item.title: Xi tells Southeast Asian leaders deeper AI cooperation is needed
item.description: Chinese President Xi Jinping on Friday urged Southeast Asian leaders to deepen cooperation on AI, days after US President Donald Trump struck deals in the region amid an intensifying technology race between the two powers. In talks with Singaporean Prime Minister Lawrence Wong on Friday, Xi said the two countries should be “development partners that lead in innovation”, adding that they should deliver results in areas ranging from the digital economy to artificial intelligence. Xi, calling China... Fuente: South China Morning Post.

item.title: 11-second handshake: Takaichi adopts more proactive approach with Xi at Apec, experts say
item.description: Exchanges between top Chinese and Japanese leaders show Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi adopting a far more proactive approach to assert control and seek direct communication, according to body language experts. Over the past two days, the Apec gala in Shenzhen has been the scene of rare in-person, high-level interactions between the two countries’ leaders, the most notable since ties between Beijing and Tokyo became severely strained over Takaichi’s remarks regarding Taiwan in November last... Fuente: South China Morning Post.

item.title: U.S. Senate approves bill to speed up permitting reviews, Democrats and environmental groups oppose
item.description: The legislation’s sweeping changes would shorten the timeline to start big energy projects and make sure data centres pay for the energy they use Fuente: The Hindu - International.

item.title: Nigeria moves to end jail terms for attempted suicide
item.description: Nigeria's proposed reform follows years of calls from psychiatrists and a parallel Senate bill. Fuente: BBC News - World.

item.title: Xi Jinping urges trust-based partnership with Australia in Shenzhen bilateral talks
item.description: China and Australia should be “partners that trust each other”, President Xi Jinping told Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese in Shenzhen on Friday. Xi struck an upbeat tone on Beijing’s relationship with Canberra, describing it as “developing steadily” now, in the meeting after the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation leaders’ summit in the southern Chinese city. “China and Australia have neither historical grievances nor fundamental conflicts of interest, and should be partners who trust... Fuente: South China Morning Post.

item.title: Calls for One Nation candidate to withdraw from election over misconduct
item.description: Anti-violence campaigners say One Nation candidate Garner Smith should not be running in the Victorian election after breaching five standards of conduct while a Gannawarra councillor. Fuente: ABC News Australia.

item.title: Tashima says Balogun red card row at World Cup prompted FIFA presidency bid
item.description: Tashima is one of three names on the ballot for the March election, along with current President Infantino and Diallo. Fuente: Al Jazeera English.

item.title: Infantino, Tashima and Diallo officially enter FIFA presidential race
item.description: Three candidates have officially submitted their bids for the FIFA presidency. Gianni Infantino, who has been in office for 11 years, is seeking a fourth consecutive term. Backed by UEFA, French Football Federation president Philippe Diallo wants to offer an alternative to Infantino’s leadership. He will face Japan’s Kozo Tashima, honorary president of the Japan Football Association. The election will take place on March 18, 2027 in Rabat, Morocco. Fuente: France 24 - English.
item.dc:creator: L'Equipe TV

item.title: Czechs protest en masse against 'concentration of power in one hand' and growing control over media
item.description: As large demonstrations in the Czech Republic challenge Prime Minister Andrej Babiš's plans to change the funding model of public broadcasters, Mikuláš Minář, Chair of the Million Moments for Democracy movement, joins François Picard from Prague for Spotlight, warning that his country risks following Hungary and Slovakia in democratic backsliding. "We are really afraid that the Czech Republic is following the Orbánian Hungarian way, (Fico's) Slovakian way," he says. Fuente: France 24 - English.
item.dc:creator: François PICARD

item.title: Gen Z Is Driving Global Political Change, Aiding Far Left and Far Right
item.description: Protests planned across Europe on Friday are the latest example of global youth anger that has driven demonstrations and election upsets. Fuente: The New York Times - World.

item.description: The permitting bill's Senate passage is a key step to it becoming law, but it would also need to clear the House before heading to President Trump's desk. Fuente: CNBC - World.

item.title: Trump nominee refuses to call Jan 6 an ‘attack’ at Senate hearing
item.description: Trump’s nominee to lead the US agency responsible for election security, refused to call the insurrection an attack. Fuente: Al Jazeera English.

item.title: ¿Qué dejó el cara a cara entre Sánchez y Feijóo a diez días de las elecciones en España?
item.description: A diez días de las elecciones generales en España, el presidente del Gobierno, Pedro Sánchez, y el líder del Partido Popular, Alberto Núñez Feijóo, protagonizaron un debate en el que ningún candidato buscó convencer sino evitar errores y que no apeló a los electores jóvenes. Para analizarlo nos acompaña Miguel Gomis, politólogo y doctor en Ciencia Política. Publicado también por: Clarín - Mundo. Fuente: France 24 - Español.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Informe desde Río de Janeiro: Lula firma decreto de reducción de jornada laboral
item.description: El presidente de Brasil, Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, firmó un decreto que reglamenta la transición de la semana laboral de seis días de trabajo y uno de descanso, a un esquema de cinco días laborales y dos de descanso. La medida, aprobada previamente por el Congreso, comenzará a aplicarse el 16 de diciembre y reducirá gradualmente la jornada máxima de 44 a 40 horas semanales para 2027. Nos amplía nuestra corresponsal Valeria Saccone. Fuente: France 24 - Español.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: EU and UK set to sign deals on trade, energy, youth mobility at Brussels summit
item.description: The UK and the EU are poised to agree new deals on trade, energy and youth mobility at a summit in Brussels on Friday, as part of UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham's bid to reset ties with the bloc. Burnham – who has said he hopes to see Britain rejoin the EU in his lifetime – argues the deals will help fix some of the damage Brexit inflicted. Fuente: France 24 - English.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE 24

item.title: "¿Qué le debe a Marruecos?": Sánchez y Núñez Feijóo chocan en su único debate cara a cara
item.description: A días de las elecciones generales del 29 de noviembre, el líder del PP, Alberto Núñez Feijóo, acusó al presidente Pedro Sánchez de no haber construido las viviendas prometidas y lo criticó por su relación con Marruecos tras la crisis migratoria en Ceuta. El socialista defendió su gestión y se mostró dispuesto a pedir perdón a las víctimas de los accidentes ferroviarios. Fuente: France 24 - Español.
item.dc:creator: France 24

item.title: El Reino Unido se acerca a la UE en una cumbre clave diez años después del Brexit
item.description: «El Brexit que nos dieron no ha funcionado. Hemos perdido más de lo que hemos ganado». Estas palabras las pronunció Andy Burnham esta semana, antes de viajar este viernes a Bruselas, donde intentará recuperar algo de lo perdido aunque sin que pueda decirse que está dando marcha atrás. Por ejemplo, su Gobierno quiere que sea más fácil vender alimentos británicos en Europa, pero no quiere volver al mercado único que hacía más fácil venderlos. A cuatro exministros laboristas esa distinción ya no les parece razón suficiente para quedarse fuera de la Unión, y dos de ellos, David Lammy y Peter… Fuente: ABC España - Internacional.
item.dc:creator: Ivannia Salazar

item.title: “Tenemos tiempo”: ¿resistirá Trump la presión de Netanyahu por retomar las hostilidades contra Irán?
item.description: El presidente estadounidense no parece tener prisa para reanudar los ataques a gran escala, a pesar de la presión por parte de Benjamin Netanyahu para lanzar una nueva campaña aérea conjunta, de la carta blanca (al menos provisional) por parte del Congreso saliente, que volvió a fracasar en el intento de limitar sus capacidades bélicas, y de sus propios anuncios de que podría volver al campo de batalla después de las midterms. Los aliados del golfo pesan sobre la posición del magnate republicano. Fuente: France 24 - Español.
item.dc:creator: Eumar Esaá

item.title: Líderes en Europa cierran filas en torno a Zelenski tras cumbre trilateral en China
item.description: Tras la histórica cumbre trilateral celebrada en Shenzhen, China, entre Donald Trump, Xi Jinping y Vladímir Putin, líderes europeos cerraron filas en torno al presidente ucraniano Volodímir Zelenski y reiteraron que cualquier negociación sobre el futuro de Ucrania debe contar con la participación de Kiev y de Europa. Durante una reunión paralela en Berlín, la llamada "Coalición de Voluntarios" reafirmó su apoyo político y de seguridad a Ucrania, en medio de la preocupación por eventuales acuerdos entre las grandes potencias sin presencia europea. Fuente: France 24 - Español.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Pete Hegseth se reúne con Noboa para revisar la cooperación en la lucha contra el narcoterrorismo en Ecuador
item.description: En una cita marcada por el hermetismo y a la que no tuvo acceso la prensa, el secretario de Guerra de Estados Unidos , Pete Hegseth, se reunió con el presidente Daniel Noboa este jueves 19 de noviembre en el palacio presidencial en Quito, en la que se supo pasaron revista a los acuerdos de cooperación contra el narcotráfico que mantiene Estados Unidos con Ecuador.Fue el secretario de Guerra quien, en su cuenta X, escribió que hablaron del compromiso compartido para hacer frente a las amenazas narcoterroristas, reforzar la seguridad fronteriza y lograr resultados decisivos para nuestra… Fuente: ABC España - Internacional.
item.dc:creator: Thalía Flores

item.title: Colombia: oposición moviliza manifestaciones contra De la Espriella en diferentes ciudades
item.description: Miles de personas participaron este 19 de noviembre en una jornada de movilizaciones convocada por centrales obreras, sindicatos, organizaciones sociales y sectores de oposición en distintas ciudades de Colombia. Las protestas fueron en rechazo al Gobierno del presidente Abelardo de la Espriella. En Cali, el expresidente Gustavo Petro acompañó las manifestaciones y llamó a mantener la movilización ciudadana. Fuente: France 24 - Español.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: PM Sánchez admits 'mistakes' in key debate ahead of Spain's election
item.description: Spain's Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez acknowledged shortcomings in his government on Thursday as he faced conservative rival Alberto Núñez Feijóo in the campaign's only televised debate. The November 29 election could leave the far-right Vox party in a position to enter government. Fuente: France 24 - English.

item.title: Trump says no rush to decide on new Iran strikes, looks to next year
item.description: US President Donald Trump on Thursday appeared to push a decision on renewed major strikes against Iran into next year, extending a timeline that he had previously suggested could come to a head after this month’s US midterm elections. Asked in an interview about the possibility of new strikes, Trump said: “Well, I’ll talk to you about it after the beginning of the year.” “We’ve got time,” ‌Trump added, speaking from his plane as he returned to Washington from his trip to China. item.title: Live: Victorian election ballots isolated after incident at voting centre
item.description: The Victorian Electoral Commission says there is no suggestion that the integrity of the vote has been compromised, after an incident saw someone gain unauthorised entry to a Richmond voting centre. Fuente: ABC News Australia.

item.title: French far-left candidate Mélenchon opens door to alliance with rival Greens candidate
item.description: French far-left leader Jean-Luc Mélenchon opened the door to an alliance with France's Greens on Thursday after their presidential candidate Marine Tondelier said she was ready to "work on a coalition around" the veteran leftist. Tondelier's overture has further boosted Mélenchon's campaign for the Élysée Palace – and angered moderates on the centre-left. Fuente: France 24 - English.

item.title: Combates en Martissant: ¿qué se sabe de la operación que dejó al menos 34 pandilleros muertos en Haití?
item.description: Al menos 34 presuntos miembros de la banda de Grand Ravine murieron este jueves 19 de noviembre en una operación de la Policía con apoyo de la empresa Vectus Global. Se trata de la primera ofensiva de gran alcance en Martissant desde que las pandillas tomaron el control de esa zona hace cinco años y cortaron la principal ruta entre Puerto Príncipe y el sur del país. Medios señalan que en la operación también intervienen soldados del contingente enviado por el presidente Nayib Bukele. Fuente: France 24 - Español.

item.title: Kushner says Trump 'open' to extend NATO mutual defense-type clause to Ukraine
item.description: US envoy Jared Kushner said Thursday that President Donald Trump was open to extending to Ukraine a security guarantee similar to NATO's mutual defense clause, but stressed that Washington has to protect its interests too. item.description: La edición 33 del Foro de Cooperación Económica Asia – Pacífico culminó en la ciudad de Shenzhen sin avances significativos en el ámbito económico, pero con material para realizar una reflexión.
